biomes.note: sea floor below the datum: rocky bed
no sand material in the proven template; partial rock stands in
no snow material in the proven template; winter snow physics comes from the template's grass layer
no ice material in the proven template

notes: Material weights for the two layers the proven terrain template provides (MMR-16: grass base at full weight, rock_k painted over it). The rock weight of a sample is max(the biome's rock, the slope rule round-half-even(clamp((slope - start) / (full - start), 0, 1) * 255)), where slope is the output grid's central-difference gradient in world units, as the encoder computes it. Every exported biome id must appear here with the same core name, and every water_type, river and landform code must be listed; anything else fails. coastEpsilon (world units) keeps the compiled coastline coherent with the sea datum: ocean samples are lowered to at most -coastEpsilon and land samples raised to at least +coastEpsilon, which survives 16-bit quantization and the engine's 0.03 truncation toward zero. Lakes are left as compiled. Version 1 ignores layers.biome_variant (magical variants): materials follow the natural biome only.
